title: 第3章 太极饕餮第4章 星火诀
content_zh:
;;
刚回山上，一个不满十岁，唇红齿白的光头小和尚跑了过来，满脸雀跃道：
“师兄，师兄！
你晓得狐狸是怎么叫的吗？”
鱼吞舟还在复盘今日从张前辈那听来的服气之说，下意识敷衍道：
“大楚兴，陈胜王。”
小沙弥瞪大眼睛，似乎受到了极大冲击。
鱼吞舟脚步未停，回到了家门前。
说是家，其实就是四堵黄泥墙支着个茅草顶，屋顶的茅絮铺得虽厚，但边缘已经有些松散了。
虽是陋室，但惟吾德馨，也不孤零。
他家左邻是座青瓦道观，观门常年半掩，里头总有个老道长趺坐，不怎么喜欢说话。
右边是一座庙宇，除了小和尚定光外，还有位法号玄苦的大师。
而这两位，就是三年前和老墨一起保下他的另外两位前辈。
鱼吞舟将两条龙鱼倒进道观门口的大水缸里，龙鱼摆尾，溅起几点水花，荡起层层涟漪，生命力顽强的可怕。
他转身回屋，把早上收进来的鱼干搬到竹匾上，重新一一悬挂在屋檐下。
“定光，生火。”
鱼吞舟往外面喊了一声，挽起袖子，向着屋后不远的菜地走去，揪了一把翠绿蔬菜，来到一旁的灶房。
灶台色泽深沉，显然有些年月了，鱼吞舟拿起一旁白腻腻的肥肉擦了擦锅子，炒了盘青菜，煎了个咸鱼。
至于米饭，定光在他训练下，已经能独立煮饭了。
小镇不生产粮食，这些米都是和寺庙借的，而菜园则是老道长的。

前者的代价，就是他要帮忙照看定光；后者则是将菜园子交给了他照看，前后也有快三年了。
午饭备好，虽然简单，但煎的焦黄的咸鱼，配上新鲜炒青菜，看上去也颇有食欲。
鱼吞舟取出两幅单独碗筷，盛了米饭，只夹上炒青菜。
一份他亲自送到了隔壁道观，另一份则由定光送去了寺庙，然后两小才开始用餐。
“师兄，咱下次腌鱼的时候能少放点盐吗？”
定光夹了一筷子鱼肉，垫了好几口白米饭，眼巴巴望来，“师兄，咱今晚能吃上鲜鱼不？”
“盐多下饭。”
鱼吞舟假装没听懂，“这不就是咸鱼吗？”
那两条龙鱼，他准备拿去镇上碰碰运气，换上一门服气法，只得先苦一苦定光了。
定光摸了摸自己的光头，道：“师兄，你是不是要开始修炼了？”
鱼吞舟喝了一大口水，心中暗自下决定，下次再腌鱼，确实要少放些盐了。
听到定光突然这么问，他不禁放下茶杯，问道：
“玄苦大师跟你说了什么吗？”
老和尚法号玄苦，是不是得道高僧，鱼吞舟不清楚，但能出现在这座小镇的，应该就没一个简单的。
只可惜，玄苦大师和道观中的守心道长，处境类似于老墨，虽然给他提供了一定庇护，但在修行一道上帮不到他分毫。
“没有啊。”
定光往嘴里塞了一大口饭，腮帮子鼓得像只小包子，含糊不清道，
“不过今早有人来拜访师父，等人走了，师父就在庙里嘀咕，说小镇又要热闹起来了。
我就猜应该是这届的仙种选拔要开始了。”
“仙种选拔？”

“师父说，最后能走出小镇的就是仙种。”
“大师还说了什么？”
“说留给你的时间不多了。”
定光殷勤道，“师兄，要不我们去求求师父，让他把你正式收入门中？”

As soon as I returned to the mountain, a bald little monk under ten years old with red lips and white teeth ran over and said with joy on his face:
“Senior brother, senior brother!
Do you know what the fox calls? "
Yu Tunzhou was still reviewing the convincing words he heard from Senior Zhang today, and subconsciously said perfunctorily:
"Great Chu is rising, King Chen Sheng."
The little novice's eyes widened, as if he was greatly shocked.
Yu Tunzhou returned to the door of his house without stopping.
It's called a home, but it's actually just four yellow mud walls supporting a thatched roof. Although the thatched roof is thick, the edges are already a little loose.
Although it is a humble house, I am virtuous and not alone.
His house's left neighbor is a Taoist temple with green tiles. The gate is always ajar, and there is always an old Taoist priest sitting inside who doesn't like to talk much.
On the right is a temple. In addition to the young monk Dingguang, there is also a master named Xuanku.
And these two are the other two seniors who worked with Lao Mo to protect him three years ago.
Yu Tunzhou poured the two arowanas into the large water tank at the entrance of the Taoist temple. The arowanas swung their tails, splashed a few splashes, and made ripples. Their vitality was terrifying.
He turned back to the house, moved the dried fish he had collected in the morning onto the bamboo plaques, and hung them one by one under the eaves again.
"Fix the light and light the fire."
Yu Tunzhou shouted outside, rolled up his sleeves, and walked towards the vegetable patch not far behind the house. He grabbed a handful of green vegetables and went to the kitchen nearby.
The stove had a dark color and was obviously old. Yu Tunzhou picked up the greasy white meat on the side and wiped the pot, stir-fried a plate of vegetables and fried salted fish.
As for rice, Dingguang was able to cook independently under his training.
The town does not produce food. The rice is borrowed from the temple, and the vegetable garden belongs to the old Taoist priest.
The price for the former was that he had to help take care of Dingguang; the latter gave him the responsibility to take care of the vegetable garden for almost three years.
Lunch was prepared. Although it was simple, the fried brown salted fish and fresh stir-fried vegetables looked quite appetizing.
Yu Tunzhou took out two separate bowls and chopsticks, filled them with rice, and only added fried vegetables.
He personally delivered one portion to the Taoist temple next door, and the other portion was delivered to the temple by Dingguang, and then he started eating two hours later.
"Brother, can we put less salt in the pickled fish next time?"
Dingguang picked up a piece of fish with chopsticks, put several mouthfuls of white rice on it, and looked eagerly, "Senior brother, can we eat fresh fish tonight?"
“The more salt goes with the rice.”
Yu Tunzhou pretended not to understand, "Isn't this just salted fish?"
He was going to take those two arowanas to the town to try his luck and use the Qi Convincing Technique, but he had to suffer a lot first.
Dingguang touched his bald head and said, "Senior brother, are you going to start practicing?"
Yu Tunzhou took a sip of water and secretly decided that next time he would pickle fish, he would definitely add less salt.
Hearing Dingguang suddenly ask this question, he couldn't help but put down his tea cup and asked:
"Did Master Xuanku tell you something?"
The old monk's Buddhist name is Xuan Ku. Whether he is an eminent monk or not, Yu Tunzhou doesn't know, but there should be no simple ones who can appear in this small town.
It's a pity that Master Xuanku and Taoist Shouxin in the Taoist temple are in a similar situation to Lao Mo. Although they provide him with some protection, they can't help him at all in his practice.
"No."
Dingguang stuffed a big mouthful of rice into his mouth, his cheeks puffed up like little buns, and he said vaguely,
“But someone came to visit Master this morning, and when they left, Master was muttering in the temple that the town was going to be lively again.
I guess the selection of immortal seeds for this session is about to begin. "
"Selection of Immortal Seeds?"
"Master said that the one who can finally walk out of the town is the immortal."
"What else did the master say?"
"Tell me you don't have much time left."
Dingguang said diligently, "Senior brother, how about we go and beg the master and let him formally accept you into the sect?"
